title: Grothendieck topos: small-site presentation
statement: Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ as in [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\operatorname{Sets}_{\mathcal V}$ be the category of sets belonging to $\mathcal V$. Let $\mathcal D$ be a category. A *sieve* on an object $d$ is a set $S$ of morphisms with target $d$ such that $f\circ g\in S$ whenever $f\in S$ and $f\circ g$ is defined; for $f:d'\to d$ put $f^*S=\{g:f\circ g\in S\}$, a sieve on $d'$. A *Grothendieck topology* $J$ on $\mathcal D$ assigns to every object $d$ a set $J(d)$ of sieves on $d$, the covering sieves, such that (i) the sieve of all morphisms with target $d$ belongs to $J(d)$; (ii) if $S\in J(d)$ and $f:d'\to d$, then $f^*S\in J(d')$; (iii) if $S\in J(d)$ and $R$ is a sieve on $d$ with $f^*R\in J(d')$ for every $f:d'\to d$ in $S$, then $R\in J(d)$. A functor $F:\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Sets}_{\mathcal V}$ is a *$J$-sheaf* if for every object $d$ and every $S\in J(d)$, each family $(s_f)_{f\in S}$ with $s_f\in F(\operatorname{dom}f)$ and $s_{f\circ g}=F(g)(s_f)$ is $(F(f)(s))_{f\in S}$ for exactly one $s\in F(d)$; $\Sh(\mathcal D,J;\operatorname{Sets}_{\mathcal V})$ is the full subcategory of the functor category on the $J$-sheaves. A category $\mathcal E$ is a *$\mathcal V$-Grothendieck topos* if it admits a *$\mathcal V$-small-site presentation*: a $\mathcal V$-small category $\mathcal D$ (its objects and its morphisms form sets in $\mathcal V$), a Grothendieck topology $J$ on $\mathcal D$, and an equivalence of categories $\mathcal E\simeq\Sh(\mathcal D,J;\operatorname{Sets}_{\mathcal V})$.
